name: section-title
purpose: The framed header row that opens a page section: an optional overline, the section's `h2`, an optional description and an optional row of actions, held inside a registration frame whose bottom rule is what divides the header from the section body. `kind` picks the layout — `centered` for a symmetric opener, `left` for a reading-order one, and `horizontal` for a wide row that sets the headline against its description.
useWhen: Opening a marketing or landing page section that needs a framed header.
Whenever the header itself should carry the rule that separates it from the content below, with no extra margin.
For a wide band whose headline and supporting sentence should sit side by side rather than stacked — `kind="horizontal"`.
avoidWhen: For the page's leading band and its `h1` → use `hero` instead.
For the top bar of an application shell → use `global-header` instead.
For a plain framed container with arbitrary content → use `frame-box` instead.
related: hero` — the opening band; its `Hero.Title` renders the page's `h1` at hero scale.
frame-box` — the frame this component composes.
section-gap` — the empty frame that sets the air before and after a section header; this component holds no vertical air of its own beyond its padding.
overline` — the eyebrow treatment rendered above the headline.
bestPractices: Leave `framed` on when the header is a brick of its own in a page column; turn it off when a band composes the header inside a frame it already draws, so the rule and the padding are not drawn twice.

Keep one `section-title` per section, and let it own the section's `h2` so the page keeps one document outline. `size` changes the headline's step on the type scale, never its heading level — a page with a `large` and a `small` header still reads as two `h2`s.

Leave `size` at `medium` for an ordinary section opener. Reach for `large` only where the headline is the band's whole statement, and for `small` where the header opens a subsection inside a band that already has one.
Write the eyebrow as one or two words: it is set uppercase and prefixed with `//`, so a sentence in it reads as noise.
Reach for `horizontal` when the description is long enough to earn its own column — on a narrow viewport it stacks back under the headline.

In `horizontal`, set `--section-title-headline-span` to `2` from the consumer's class to run the headline across the middle column too, when it would otherwise wrap to three lines; the description keeps the third column, and the default `1` leaves that column as air. `--section-title-headline-max` caps the headline's width inside its span (`none` by default), so a headline that would fit on one line across two columns still breaks into two.

In `horizontal`, set `descriptionWidth="wide"` when the description runs to a paragraph and would stack six or more lines in the third column alone; it then spans the middle and third columns, capped at `--container-xl` and aligned to the right edge so it ends where the narrow description ends. It takes the column a `--section-title-headline-span` of `2` would claim, so use one or the other. Outside `horizontal` the prop has no effect.
Put the section's CTAs in the `actions` slot rather than in the body; the slot already stacks them fluid below `sm` and aligns them with the chosen `kind` above it.
The vertical rhythm around the header belongs to the `section-gap` frames on either side, not to this component.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the section, rendered as the section's `h2`.

props.name: description
props.doc: Supporting sentence under the headline; overridden by the default slot.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Short uppercase overline rendered above the headline.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Layout of the header: `centered` stacks and centers the copy, `left` stacks it at the start edge, `horizontal` sets the headline and its description in two columns.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the headline on the heading scale: `small` for a subsection inside a band, `medium` for an ordinary section opener, `large` for a band whose headline is the statement.

props.name: framed
props.doc: Draw the header's own frame and padding. Turn it off when the header is composed inside a band that already owns both.

props.name: padding
props.doc: Vertical padding of the framed header: `medium` for a section opener, `small` for a header that sits tight over its band.

props.name: descriptionWidth
props.doc: Width of the description in the horizontal layout: `narrow` keeps it to the third column, `wide` runs it across the middle column too.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Description body; replaces the `description` prop when provided.

slots.name: actions
slots.notes: Call-to-action row under the copy, aligned with the chosen `kind`.
